title: be/have/do in present and past tenses
subtitle: am/is/are, was/were, have/has, do/does/did
summary: Learn which helping verb goes with -ing, with a past participle and with the infinitive, in the present and in the past.

lesson.heading: be + -ing
lesson.text: **am/is/are + -ing** is the present continuous: the action is happening now. **was/were + -ing** is the past continuous: the action was happening at a time in the past.

examples.text: It **wasn't raining**, so we didn't need an umbrella.

lesson.heading: be + past participle
lesson.text: **am/is/are + past participle** is the passive present. **was/were + past participle** is the passive past. The past participle is **cleaned**, **made**, **eaten**, **born** etc.

lesson.heading: have/has + past participle
lesson.text: **have/has + past participle** is the present perfect. We use it for things that have happened up to now.

lesson.heading: do/does/did + infinitive
lesson.text: **do/does + infinitive** makes present simple negatives and questions. **did + infinitive** makes past simple negatives and questions. After do/does/did the verb has no ending.

examples.text: I like coffee, but I **don't like** tea.
What time **did** Paul and Nicole **go** out?

lesson.heading: Which helping verb, and what comes after it
rows: Butter is made from milk. The office was cleaned.
I've cleaned my room. Tom has lost his passport.
I don't like tea. Did you go out?

lesson.text: Use **is/are** with **-ing** and with a past participle, but never with **do**: say *Is Maria working?* or *Does Maria work?*, not ~~Does Maria working?~~

exercises.explanation: looking is an -ing form, so it needs are: Why are you looking at me?
live is the infinitive, and Bill = he, so we use Does.
shining is an -ing form and the sun = it, so we use Is.

exercises.prompt: Match each helping verb with the sentence that uses it.

pairs.right: I was working when she arrived.
What time did Paul go out?

exercises.prompt: Gary ___ working this week. He's on holiday.
exercises.explanation: working is an -ing form, so the negative is isn't working.

exercises.prompt: Nicole has travelled a lot, but she ___ speak any foreign languages.
exercises.explanation: speak is the infinitive, and she needs doesn't.
go is the infinitive and last night is past, so we use Did.
born is a past participle and your mother is one person: Where was your mother born?
arrived here is a past participle with yet, so we use Has (present perfect).

exercises.prompt: I ___ just made some coffee. Would you like some?
exercises.explanation: made is a past participle after I, so we use have (present perfect).

exercises.prompt: Which pattern does each sentence use?

items.text: It wasn't raining, so we didn't need an umbrella.
These houses were built 100 years ago.

exercises.statement: I don't know how to say this word. How is it pronounce?
exercises.explanation: How is it pronounced? After is we need the past participle pronounced.
